methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective cohort (n=776 gastric cancer patients) analyzing HBV infection (300 HBV+ including chronic/occult) vs liver metastasis (GCLM) risk. Propensity score matching (PSM) for age/gender adjustment. Univariate/multivariate logistic regression. Chi-square testing for associations. Limitations: retrospective design, potential confounding by HBV-related liver disease factors, incomplete HBV testing details.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective cohort study (LoE 2b) identifying HBV as independent GCLM risk factor (OR 2.563). Clinical relevance for surveillance strategies in HBV+ GC patients. However, mechanism unexplored and OS not improved despite GCLM risk.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE-aligned reporting: patient selection, HBV classification (chronic vs occult), outcomes clearly defined. PSM methodology described. Results with frequencies, ORs, CIs presented. Limitations: incomplete HBV testing protocol; no data repository statement.

novelty_literature.justification: First study specifically examining HBV-GCLM association in gastric cancer. HBV-hepatocellular carcinoma link established; HBV-colorectal metastasis reported; this represents extension to GC without novel mechanism.

writing_presentation.justification: Organized retrospective analysis addressing understudied HBV-metastasis association. Methods and results clearly presented. Discussion contextualizes findings. Publication-ready structure.

key_strengths: Novel HBV-gastric cancer liver metastasis association identified: 25.3% GCLM in HBV+ vs 15.8% in HBV- (p=0.001), persisting after PSM
Independent predictor in multivariable analysis (OR 2.563, p<0.001); both chronic and occult HBV showed effect
Propensity score matching adjusts for age/gender confounding
key_concerns: Retrospective single-center design with treatment heterogeneity; potential confounding by HBV-related liver disease severity, cirrhosis status (not analyzed)
Mechanism unexplored: 'seed and soil' hypothesis discussed theoretically without experimental validation or molecular evidence
OS unchanged between HBV+/- groups (p=0.737) despite higher GCLM in HBV+ patients, questioning clinical significance of increased metastasis risk
Limited actionability: surveillance recommendation without specific intervention studies
chief_reviewer.rationale: Retrospective observational study identifying novel HBV-GCLM association but with unclear mechanism and unchanged OS. Appropriate for tier 4 specialty journals with recommendations for mechanistic follow-up studies.
